provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
In the native task, a square input g becomes a 4x4 arrangement of g-sized blocks. The output has four 2x2-tiled quadrants: top-left is g rotated 180 degrees, top-right is g rotated clockwise, bottom-left is g rotated counter-clockwise, and bottom-right is g unchanged.

The visible transform T is applied to both input and output. It does two things:
1. It moves the quadrants around. Applying T to the 2x2 grid of quadrant ids gives which native quadrant now sits at each visible position.
2. It changes each tiled block into T(R(g)), which equals (T R T^-1)(G) for the visible input G. For rotation elements (d4<4) this is the same rotation R. For reflection elements (d4>=4) it is the inverse rotation.

The factory works out these four (quadrant position, rot90 turn count) constants at build time. The emitted program then rotates the visible input directly by each constant and tiles it 2x2 into the matching visible quadrant. It does not un-transform the input or re-transform the output.

Colours are copied cell by cell, so no palette constants are needed. Every output cell is overwritten, so the background fill colour never shows in the result.
draft_notes.limitations: The constructor only produces 3x3 inputs, and the mechanism needs square inputs: a rotated non-square block would not fit its quadrant. The emitted program assumes a square input. I found no constructor defects, ties, or fixture contradictions, and the fixtures match the uniform rule. I have not executed the factory or the emitted program.

independent_source_review.mechanism: A 3x3 input becomes a 12x12 output made of four 6x6 quadrants. Each quadrant is one rotation of the input tiled 2x2. Native layout: top-left is 180°, top-right is clockwise (rot90 k=3), bottom-left is counter-clockwise (k=1), bottom-right is identity (k=0). For augmentation T, the factory permutes the quadrant ids with the same D4 map applied to the grids. It keeps each rotation's turn count for rotation elements and negates it mod 4 for reflection elements, because T R T^-1 = R^-1 when T is a reflection. The emitted solver rotates the visible input by each baked constant and tiles it into the matching visible quadrant.
evidence: Constructor branch r>1,c>1: rr=r*3+row, cc=c*3+col. This is the identity block in tile rows/cols 2-3, i.e. the bottom-right quadrant.

Branch r<2,c>1: rr=c*3+2-col, cc=r*3+row. The block row index c is in {2,3} and the block column index r is in {0,1}, so this is the bottom-left quadrant. Locally B[2-col][row]=g[row][col], so B[i][j]=g[j][2-i], which equals np.rot90(g,1) (CCW). This matches the rule. The swapped r/c naming is not a bug.
Branch r>1,c<2: rr=c*3+col, cc=r*3+2-row. This is the top-right quadrant. Locally B[i][j]=g[2-j][i], which equals np.rot90(g,-1) (CW).
Else branch: B[2-row][2-col]=g[row][col]. This is the 180° block in the top-left quadrant.
Coverage: 16 tiles of 9 cells write all 144 cells. The background canvas is never visible.

Fixture pair 1 checks out. Top-left 1 5 8/8 8 7/8 7 8 is the 180° rotation. Top-right 8 7 8/5 8 7/1 8 8 is the CW rotation. Bottom-left 8 8 1/7 8 5/8 7 8 is the CCW rotation. Bottom-right is the identity. The test fixture also matches.

Factory native_k={0:2,1:3,2:1,3:0} matches the constructor. D4 acts on the 12x12 grid as a permutation of the four quadrants plus the same D4 applied inside each block. 2x2 tiling of a square block commutes with D4. So the visible quadrant content is tile(T R T^-1 G), which justifies the k → -k mod 4 step for reflections.
Sampler: the loop requires len(set(colors))==len(subset)+1. So every subset colour appears and at least one non-8 cell exists. Colours are copied cell by cell, so the unused palette argument is fine.
The emitted solver uses np.rot90(g,k) and slices directly in visible coordinates. There is no untransform/native-solve/retransform wrapper. It specializes only the four rule-orientation constants.
Host audit passed 1000 fresh pairs, 8000 augmented checks and 16 fixture variants with no sampler rejections.
nonblocking_limits: The solver assumes a square input, because y0/x0 come from the rotated block shape. The constructor only emits 3x3 inputs, so this lies outside the domain.
The background computation in the emitted program is dead code, since every cell is overwritten. It is harmless.

The quadrant id permutation relies on the factory's _apply_d4 convention (reflect-then-rotate-clockwise) matching the host's augmentation convention. The reflection sign flip does not depend on this convention, but the id permutation does. The passing 8000 augmented checks are consistent with a match, but I could not verify it from source.

Fresh episodes whose demonstration inputs are all highly symmetric (e.g. sparse single-colour layouts) could leave the quadrant rotations weakly identified from the demos. This is about episode identifiability, not label correctness. The context policy's D4-conflict rejection is supposed to cover it.
required_context_checks: Confirm that the host D4 index convention for d4 0-7 matches the factory's _apply_d4: horizontal flip (row reversal) for d4>=4, then d4%4 clockwise quarter-turns.

Confirm that the D4-conflict episode rejection is applied to generated episodes where every demonstration input is invariant under some non-identity D4 element, so the quadrant orientation constants stay identifiable from visible demos.

draft_notes.host_review: Read mechanism, evidence, limitations and context requirements. Host reflects columns before clockwise rotation, tests all eight D4 indices, and applies a shared palette permutation after generation. Fixture audit verifies all train/test supplied pairs at every tested orientation/palette, not one pair per variant. Per-episode execution verification and conflicting-context rejection remain required.
